title: Netflix releases trailer for Brad Bird's Ray Gunn
gist: Netflix released the trailer for Brad Bird's Ray Gunn, a neo-noir sci-fi animated feature aimed at an older audience, premiering on Netflix December 18 after a limited 70mm theatrical run from December 4. The project sat for ~30 years in a Warner Brothers filing cabinet before landing at Netflix.

insights.claim: Netflix will premiere Brad Bird's animated neo-noir sci-fi film Ray Gunn on December 18, preceded by a limited 70mm theatrical run in select theaters starting December 4.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: A prestige-director holiday release; the limited theatrical window reflects Netflix's selective use of cinemas for marquee titles.
insights.locator: Ray Gunn premieres on Netflix on December 18.

insights.claim: The Ray Gunn script, co-written with Matthew Robbins, sat in a Warner Brothers filing cabinet for about 30 years before the film was made for Netflix.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: Streamers are picking up long-shelved projects from established studios' libraries, a talent/IP sourcing channel for Netflix.
insights.quote: stayed in a filing cabinet at Warner Brothers,
insights.locator: Bird has been kicking around the idea for Ray Gunn

insights.claim: Unlike Bird's Pixar work, Ray Gunn targets a slightly older demographic with more mature themes, described as a mashup of The Maltese Falcon and Buck Rogers.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: Tests demand for adult-skewing feature animation on streaming.

insights.claim: Ray Gunn features an all-star voice cast led by Sam Rockwell and Scarlett Johansson, with Tom Waits, Matt Berry, Bobby Cannavale, Alan Tudyk and Patton Oswalt.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: Heavy talent investment signals Netflix positioning it as a major holiday title.
insights.locator: In addition to Rockwell and Johansson
